hints: Focus on what alkaline iodine does, it is the iodoform reagent that oxidises a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group to a carboxylate plus $\text{CHI}_3$.
Notice that to finish with two $\text{-COOH}$ groups after acidification, Y must supply two iodoform-positive ends with only $\text{CH}_2$ groups left between them.
Check which pentanediol has a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ unit at both ends separated by a $\text{CH}_2$ group, so both $\text{CH}_3$ carbons are lost as $\text{CHI}_3$.
walkthrough:
**Recall the iodoform oxidation**

Alkaline $\text{I}_2$ gives a yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$ with $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$. The chemistry is oxidation plus cleavage.

$$\text{R-CH(OH)-CH}_3 + 4\text{OH}^- + 3\text{I}_2 \rightarrow \text{R-COO}^- + \text{CHI}_3 + 3\text{I}^- + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Apply to a diol to get a diacid**

To get $\text{HOOC-R-COOH}$ after acidification, the alkaline product must be $\text{^-OOC-R-COO}^-$. That means Y must have an oxidisable $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group at each end of the chain.

So both terminal carbons must be $\text{CH}_3$ attached to $\text{CH(OH)}$, and what remains in the middle must be only $\text{CH}_2$ groups.

**Test pentan-2,4-diol**

Pentan-2,4-diol is $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH(OH)-CH}_2\text{-CH(OH)-CH}_3$. It has two identical $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ units.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{^-OOC-CH}_2\text{-COO}^- + 2\text{CHI}_3$$

On acidification this gives $\text{HOOC-CH}_2\text{-COOH}$, propanedioic acid, where R is one $\text{CH}_2$ group. This fits perfectly.

options.A: Pentan-1,4-diol is $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$. Only the C-4 end is iodoform positive. Reaction gives $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-$, which acidifies to a hydroxy-monocarboxylic acid, not a dicarboxylic acid.
options.B: Pentan-1,5-diol is $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. It contains only primary alcohol groups with no $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ unit, so it gives no iodoform reaction with alkaline $\text{I}_2$.
options.C: Pentan-2,3-diol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Only the C-2 end is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$. Oxidation gives $\text{^-OOC-CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, which acidifies to a hydroxy acid containing a $\text{CH(OH)}$ group, not $\text{HOOC-R-COOH}$ with R as only $\text{CH}_2$.
options.D: Pentan-2,4-diol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$. Both ends are $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, so both react to give $\text{CHI}_3$ and leave $\text{^-OOC-CH}_2\text{-COO}^-$. Acidification gives $\text{HOOC-CH}_2\text{-COOH}$ where R is $\text{CH}_2$, exactly as described.
